newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates rise on central bank NCD issue.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates rise on central bank NCD issue.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates rose at mid-session on Monday as the central bank continued its recent pattern of issuing negotiable certificates of deposit to mop up excess market liquidity, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate was at 6.070 percent against Friday's 5.987 close, still outside the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone, with 30-day commercial paper at 6.00-6.10 percent against 6.00-6.05.
The central bank said it would issue T$3 billion NCDs later on Monday.
The bank had issued NCDs almost daily in recent weeks to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say had been fuelling a dramatic 1997 stock market rally, dealers said.
Its NCD issuance has slowed since the stock market suffered a 600-point late March correction due to a hog farm epidemic and a government ban halting Taiwan's huge pork exports.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 bond yield was at 6.1010-6.1070 percent against 6.0950.
